request: how does a lever let you lift a heavy rock?

beats.intent: A plank resting on a triangular pivot, a rock on the short end
beats.narration: Rest a plank on a pivot, with a heavy rock on the short end.
beats.code:
stage.title("A lever")
pivot = draw_polygon(stage, [(-3.0, -1.6), (-2.4, -0.6), (-1.8, -1.6)], color=GREY_B, fill=0.6)
beam = draw_line(stage, (-3.6, -0.6), (2.2, -0.6), color=ORANGE)
rock = draw_circle(stage, radius=0.5, color=GREY_B, fill=0.7)
rock.move_to([-3.1, -0.1, 0])
stage.label(rock, "600 N", direction=UP)

beats.intent: Distances 0.5 m from the pivot to the rock and 3 m to the hand marked
beats.narration: The rock sits half a metre from the pivot. Your hand pushes three metres away.
beats.code:
d1 = draw_arrow(stage, (-2.4, -2.3), (-3.1, -2.3), color=GREEN, label="0.5 m")
d2 = draw_arrow(stage, (-2.4, -2.9), (1.8, -2.9), color=BLUE, label="3 m")

beats.intent: A small 100 N push arrow pressing down on the long end
beats.narration: So a push of just one hundred newtons balances the rock.
Force times distance is the same on both sides: three hundred.

request: how does GPS work out where I am?

beats.intent: One satellite dot with a circle around it at its measured distance
beats.narration: One satellite tells you how far away you are. You are somewhere on this circle.
beats.code:
stage.title("Finding you from three distances")
k, down = 0.55, np.array([0, -0.5, 0])
you = np.array([0.4, -0.6, 0]) * k + down
sats = [np.array(p) * k + down for p in ([-3.2, 0.6, 0], [2.8, 1.0, 0], [0.6, -3.0, 0])]
cols = [BLUE, GREEN, ORANGE]
s1 = Dot(sats[0], color=cols[0], radius=0.12)
c1 = Circle(radius=np.linalg.norm(sats[0] - you), color=cols[0]).move_to(sats[0])
stage.play(FadeIn(s1), Create(c1))
stage.add(s1, c1)

beats.intent: A second satellite's circle crossing the first at two points
beats.narration: A second satellite gives a second circle. They cross in just two places.
beats.code:
s2 = Dot(sats[1], color=cols[1], radius=0.12)
c2 = Circle(radius=np.linalg.norm(sats[1] - you), color=cols[1]).move_to(sats[1])
stage.play(FadeIn(s2), Create(c2))
stage.add(s2, c2)

beats.intent: A third circle through only one of those points, marked 'you'
beats.narration: A third circle passes through only one of them. That point is you.
beats.code:
s3 = Dot(sats[2], color=cols[2], radius=0.12)
c3 = Circle(radius=np.linalg.norm(sats[2] - you), color=cols[2]).move_to(sats[2])
stage.play(FadeIn(s3), Create(c3))
stage.add(s3, c3)
me = Dot(you, color=RED, radius=0.14)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(me))
stage.add(me)
stage.label(me, "you", direction=RIGHT, color=RED)

beats.intent: The three circles meeting at one point, caption about distance = speed × time
beats.narration: Each distance comes from timing a radio signal: distance is the speed of light times the delay.
beats.code:
stage.caption("distance = speed of light × signal delay")
highlight(stage, me, color=RED)

request: how much paint do I need for a 5 m by 3 m wall with a window?

beats.intent: A 5 by 3 rectangle for the wall with its sides labelled
beats.narration: The wall is five metres wide and three metres high.
beats.code:
stage.title("Painting a wall")
wall = draw_rectangle(stage, width=5, height=3, color=BLUE, fill=0.35)
stage.label(wall, "5 m", direction=DOWN)
stage.label(wall, "3 m", direction=LEFT)

beats.intent: A 1.5 by 1 window cut out of the wall
beats.narration: Take out the window, one and a half metres by one.
beats.code:
win = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=1, color=WHITE, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).move_to(wall.get_center() + np.array([0.8, 0.3, 0]))
stage.play(FadeIn(win))
stage.add(win)
stage.label(win, "1.5 m × 1 m", direction=UP)

beats.narration: Fifteen square metres, less one and a half, leaves thirteen and a half to paint.

beats.intent: Two coats at 10 m² per litre: 27 ÷ 10 = 2.7 litres
beats.narration: Two coats double it to twenty seven square metres. At ten per litre, that's 2.7 litres.

request: why is it hotter in summer than winter?

beats.intent: A yellow sun in the middle and the Earth at two sides of its orbit
beats.narration: The Earth circles the Sun once a year.
beats.code:
stage.title("Why seasons happen")
sun = Circle(radius=0.7, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to([0, -0.4, 0])
orbit = Ellipse(width=9, height=3, color=GREY_B, stroke_opacity=0.5).move_to([0, -0.4, 0])
e1 = Circle(radius=0.35, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to([-4.5, -0.4, 0])
e2 = Circle(radius=0.35, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to([4.5, -0.4, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(sun), Create(orbit), FadeIn(e1), FadeIn(e2))
stage.add(sun, orbit, e1, e2)
stage.label(sun, "Sun", direction=DOWN, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: Both Earths with an axis tilted the same way, 23.5°
beats.narration: Its axis is tilted by twenty three and a half degrees, and it always leans the same way.
beats.code:
tilt = 23.5 * DEGREES
d = np.array([np.sin(tilt), np.cos(tilt), 0]) * 0.7
a1 = Line(e1.get_center() - d, e1.get_center() + d, color=WHITE)
a2 = Line(e2.get_center() - d, e2.get_center() + d, color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(a1), Create(a2))
stage.add(a1, a2)
stage.label(e2, "23.5°", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: The left Earth's north leaning toward the Sun labelled summer, the right one leaning away labelled winter
beats.narration: Here the north leans toward the Sun: northern summer. Half a year later, across the orbit, it leans away: winter.
beats.code:
stage.label(e1, "N summer", direction=UP, color=ORANGE)
stage.label(e2, "N winter", direction=UP, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: Bars of daylight hours in London: 16.5 in June, 8 in December
beats.narration: Leaning in means steeper sunlight and longer days: in London, sixteen and a half hours in June, eight in December.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [16.5, 8], labels=["June", "December"])
stage.caption("Hours of daylight in London")
